newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: SHARES EASE IN DULL TRADE.
newsitem.headline: SHARES EASE IN DULL TRADE.

text.p: Lithuanian shares eased in dull trade on Thursday and dealers said they did not anticipate the market to really pick up for at least a few weeks.

"Things are slow now, but the market should become more active soon...The Estonian market seems to have hit its peak, and there are signals that investors from there will soon switch to Lithuania," one dealer told Reuters.
"Lithuania is a larger market and has more investment opportunities," he added.
Dealers also say that investors are biding their time pending the outcomes of a spate of shareholders' meetings.
The Litin A index fell by 13.50 points to 2,573.91 in central market trade of only 906,000 litas.
Blue chip losers included Birzai Dairy, which fell to 10.10 litas from 10.50 litas in trade of 10,100 litas.
The company said earlier today that it expected a 1997 profit of 12 to 14 million litas versus 1.9 million litas in 1996.
Its profit for the first two months of this year was 700,000 litas, double the figure for the same period last year.
Lithuania Gas slipped to 2.36 litas from 2.37 litas in trade of over 350,000 litas.
Dealers say that Lithuania Gas looks set to make some gains as investors consider getting a piece of it now before the state sells its majority stake.
Mazeikiu Nafta oil refinery slid over 14 percent to 11.11 litas in trade of 31,719 litas.
Medienos Plaushas also eased, inching down by .07 percent to 13.50 litas.
Electronics components producer Vilniaus Vingis' price rose to 5.90 litas from 5.50 litas in trade worth almost 26,000 litas.
Dealers were bullish about its prospects, saying the company's future looked good as it sought international partners and markets.
Vilniaus Bank continued to ease despite Monday's release of its 1996 results, which showed a huge leap in its net profit to 24.4 million litas from 2.9 million litas the previous year.
Its ordinary shares fell to 225.00 litas from 234.00 litas in trade of 4,500 litas while its preferential shares dropped to 1,550 litas from 1,600 litas in turnover of over 10,000 litas.
